chapter.title: Kinematics and Dynamics
chapter.scopeNote: Original condensed MCAT Physics, Mathematics and Research Reasoning lessons. Models and calculations use stated assumptions. Independent scientific review is pending; this is not exhaustive textbook coverage.

steps.text: SI units connect measurements to dimensions: kilograms for mass, meters for length and seconds for time. A number without its unit does not fully specify a physical measurement.
Derived units combine base units. A newton is kg·m/s², a joule is N·m and a pascal is N/m². Dimensional agreement is a necessary check on an equation, not proof of its numerical coefficient.
Convert with factors equal to one and cancel units explicitly. A squared length conversion squares the whole factor: one square centimeter is 10⁻⁴ square meters, not 10⁻².
Keep mass distinct from weight, and prefix scales distinct from powers. Use dimensional analysis to reject a proposed result before spending time on arithmetic.

steps.text: A scalar has magnitude; a vector also has direction. Mass and energy are scalars, while displacement, velocity, acceleration and force are vectors.
For a vector A at angle θ measured from positive x, Ax = A cos θ and Ay = A sin θ. Components carry signs determined by direction relative to the chosen axes.
Add vectors by adding corresponding components. Magnitudes generally cannot be added directly unless the vectors point along the same direction.
Perpendicular components of 3 and 4 units give a magnitude of 5 units by the Pythagorean theorem. A negative component is a direction statement, not a negative vector magnitude.

steps.text: Displacement is final position minus initial position. Distance is total path length. Returning to a starting point gives zero displacement even when distance traveled is substantial.
Average velocity is displacement divided by elapsed time; average speed is distance divided by elapsed time. Instantaneous velocity is the slope of a position-versus-time graph.
A zero average velocity does not imply zero velocity at every instant. Keep the coordinate origin and positive direction explicit when interpreting a signed result.
The area under a velocity-versus-time graph gives signed displacement. Sections below the time axis contribute negatively rather than adding to positive distance.

steps.text: Acceleration is the change in velocity per unit time. A change in direction is an acceleration even if speed remains constant.
In an inertial frame, the net external force obeys ΣF = ma for a constant-mass object. Draw all forces on the chosen object and sum them as vectors.
A force changes velocity, not necessarily motion in the force direction at that instant. An object moving right can accelerate left while slowing down.
Kinetic friction is often modeled as μkN; static friction adjusts up to a maximum μsN. Do not set static friction equal to its maximum unless impending slip is specified.

steps.text: Newton’s first law describes constant velocity when net force is zero in an inertial frame. Rest is only one possible constant-velocity state.
Newton’s second law relates net force on one object to that object’s acceleration. More individual forces do not necessarily mean a larger net force.
Third-law partners are equal and opposite forces acting on different objects. Weight and normal force on the same block are not a third-law pair.
A contact force can change without changing gravitational weight. An accelerating elevator alters apparent weight, measured by the normal force, while mg stays approximately fixed.

steps.text: For constant acceleration in one dimension, v = v0 + at and Δx = v0t + ½at². Choose signed values along one consistent axis.
The relation v² = v0² + 2aΔx eliminates time. The mean of initial and final velocity equals average velocity only when acceleration is constant over the interval.
Near Earth’s surface, free fall can be approximated with constant downward g when air resistance is negligible. At the top of a vertical toss, velocity is zero but acceleration is still downward.
For projectile motion without drag, horizontal acceleration is zero while vertical acceleration is -g if up is positive. Components share the same flight time.

application.title: 1.6 · Apply the model within its limits
paragraphs: For projectile motion without drag, horizontal acceleration is zero while vertical acceleration is -g if up is positive. Components share the same flight time.
Constant acceleration with zero initial velocity gives Δx = ½at² = ½(2)(3²) = +9 m.

steps.text: Translational equilibrium requires zero net force. Rotational equilibrium requires zero net torque about an axis; complete static equilibrium requires both.
Torque magnitude is rF sin θ, or force times its perpendicular lever arm. A force applied through the pivot has zero torque about that pivot.
Choose a rotation sign convention before summing torques. Equal force magnitudes can produce different torques when lever arms differ.
A freely rotating ideal seesaw balances when clockwise and counterclockwise torques cancel. Equilibrium does not require every individual force or torque to vanish.

paragraphs: Translational equilibrium requires zero net force. Rotational equilibrium requires zero net torque about an axis; complete static equilibrium requires both.
Torque magnitude is rF sin θ, or force times its perpendicular lever arm. A force applied through the pivot has zero torque about that pivot.
